about_intro: kloPIT is a free, open-source PIT-38 tax calculator designed to help Polish investors calculate capital gains tax from foreign brokers.
about_name_origin: The name "kloPIT" comes from the Ukrainian word "клопіт" and the Polish "kłopot" — both meaning worry, hassle, or trouble. Because filing taxes from foreign brokers is exactly that kind of headache. This tool takes the hassle out of the equation so you can focus on investing, not paperwork.

docs_ibi_rsu_step4: In kloPIT go to Data → Import and drop the PDFs — you can import several at once

If your plan is non-qualifying, adjust the cost basis manually.
docs_ibi_rsu_tip2: For RSUs vested in earlier years but sold this year, add a carry-in position on the Data page with cost basis 0 and the original vesting date so FIFO picks it up.

docs_ibi_step4: In kloPIT go to Data → Import and drop the PDFs — you can import several at once
docs_ibi_tip1: IBI issues one PDF per ESPP order, so a year with several sales will produce several PDFs — import them all together.
docs_ibi_tip2: Each PDF contains both the grant (buy) and execution (sell); kloPIT uses Price For Tax as the PL cost basis for that ESPP lot.
docs_ibkr_w8ben_detect_body: If a dividend row on the Dashboard shows a ⚠ warning, kloPIT detected withholding above the treaty cap (15% for US issuers). The excess is not creditable against your Polish tax.
docs_ibkr_w8ben_intro_body: W-8BEN is a US tax form that certifies you are a non-US tax resident. Filing it with your broker unlocks the reduced Poland–US treaty withholding rate (15%) on US dividends, instead of the default 30% backup withholding.
docs_ibkr_w8ben_renewal_note: W-8BEN expires every 3 years. A lapsed form is the most common cause of a sudden jump back to 30% withholding mid-year — re-submit before expiry.
docs_ibkr_w8ben_where_body: In IBKR Client Portal, open Settings → Account Settings → Tax Forms and submit/renew W-8BEN. Your broker handles the filing — you do not send the form to the IRS yourself.
docs_ibkr_w8ben_where_title: Where to find it in IBKR
docs_ibkr_w8ben_why_body: Poland credits foreign withholding only up to the treaty cap (15% for US). Any excess (e.g., 30% vs 15%) is not recoverable in Poland — you'd have to reclaim it from the IRS directly. kloPIT applies this cap automatically (see src/core/tax/treaty-rates.ts).
docs_more_brokers_coming: More brokers are on the roadmap (Trading 212, DEGIRO, Revolut). The parser plugin architecture lives in src/core/parsers/ — contributions and PRs are welcome.
faq_01_answer: kloPIT is a free, open-source tax calculator for Polish investors who need to file a PIT-38 form for income from foreign brokerage accounts. It helps you calculate capital gains and dividend taxes, taking into account currency conversions and FIFO cost basis accounting.
faq_02_answer: No. kloPIT is a tool to help you with calculations, but it is not official tax software and does not submit anything to the tax office. You are responsible for verifying the results and filing your PIT-38 and PIT/ZG forms yourself, for example, through the e-Urząd Skarbowy portal.
faq_02_question: Does kloPIT file my taxes for me?
faq_03_answer: All data you import or enter is processed locally in your browser. Your financial information never leaves your computer and is not sent to any server.
faq_04_answer: Currently, kloPIT supports importing CSV activity statements from Interactive Brokers. We plan to add support for more brokers in the future. You can also add transactions manually.
faq_05_answer: kloPIT uses the official daily average exchange rates published by the National Bank of Poland (NBP). It automatically fetches the correct rate for the business day preceding each transaction.
faq_05_question: How are currency exchange rates handled?
faq_06_answer: Capital gains are calculated with the FIFO (First In, First Out) method required for pooled brokerage accounts. Each sell is matched to your oldest buy lots first. Cost basis includes buy price plus buy commission, while sell commission reduces proceeds.
faq_06_question: How are buy and sell trades matched?
faq_07_answer: Amounts in foreign currencies are converted to PLN using the NBP average rate from the last business day before the transaction date. Trades use rates for both trade amount and commission. Dividends and withholding taxes are also converted with their own applicable rates.
faq_07_question: How are PLN values calculated from USD/EUR transactions?
faq_08_answer: For each dividend, kloPIT caps the creditable foreign withholding tax at the lower of the Polish domestic rate (19%) and the bilateral tax-treaty (UPO) rate for the issuer's country — for example 15% for US, Germany, France, and Netherlands, or 10% for the UK and Japan. Countries without a mapped treaty fall back to the 19% domestic cap. Any excess withholding on one dividend cannot reduce tax due on another dividend, and excess above the treaty rate is never deductible in Poland — recover it from the foreign tax authority if needed.
faq_08_question: How is foreign withholding tax deducted for dividends?
faq_09_answer: kloPIT maps results to PIT-38 fields step by step: proceeds and costs in Section C, tax base and capital gains tax in Section D, dividend tax summary in Section G, payment summary, and the optional OPP request in Section J. It also builds PIT/ZG C.3 values per country for share income, using ISIN country mapping and reusing dividend ISIN mappings for the same symbol when needed.
faq_09_question: How are PIT-38 and PIT/ZG fields calculated?
faq_10_answer: Fields marked as rounded to full PLN, such as the tax base and tax due, use standard mathematical rounding. PIT-38 fields shown in zł/gr, including Section C totals and payment summary lines 51-52, keep grosz precision. Dividend flat-tax difference fields are rounded up to full grosz where required by the form rules.
faq_10_question: What rounding rules does kloPIT apply?
faq_11_answer: Sections E and F (crypto) and monthly flat-rate fields in sections H/I are currently placeholders in kloPIT and are set to zero. The app currently focuses on capital gains and foreign dividends for PIT-38 with PIT/ZG support.

page_pit38_h1: PIT-38 — form, instructions, downloadable PDF and online filing
page_pit38_intro: PIT-38 is the Polish annual return for capital income (art. 30b of the PIT Act). This guide explains who must file it, the deadlines, where to download the form, and how to fill it in step by step — including online, for free, using kloPIT.
page_pit38_meta_description: What is PIT-38, who files it, when, and how to fill each section. Deadlines, legal basis, and links to official forms.
page_pit38_meta_title: PIT-38 {year} — form, instructions, downloadable PDF | kloPIT
page_pit38_sec1_body: PIT-38 is the tax return filed by individuals who realized income from the sale of securities (shares, ETFs, bonds) or received foreign dividends. The current version in force is PIT-38(18) (for tax year 2024 and later). The form covers section C (securities sales), section D (capital gains tax calculation), section G (foreign dividends), section J (optional 1.5% OPP request), and the PIT/ZG attachment for foreign-sourced share income.
page_pit38_sec2_b1: You sold shares, ETFs or other securities outside of a business activity.
page_pit38_sec2_b2: You invest with a foreign broker (Interactive Brokers, XTB, Trading 212, IBI Capital) and will not receive a PIT-8C — you are responsible for reporting the income yourself.
page_pit38_sec2_b3: You received foreign dividends — they must be reported in section G, even if the broker withheld tax at source.
page_pit38_sec2_b4: You realized a capital loss — worth declaring, since it reduces tax in the following 5 years (art. 9 sec. 3 PIT Act).
page_pit38_sec3_body: The filing deadline and tax payment date is April 30 of the year following the tax year. PIT-38 for {year} must be filed by {deadline}. The form is submitted electronically (e-Urząd Skarbowy, e-Deklaracje) or on paper at the competent tax office.
page_pit38_sec3_title: Deadlines — PIT-38 for {year} and subsequent years
page_pit38_sec4_c: Section C — proceeds and costs from the sale of securities (art. 30b sec. 1). Foreign broker data goes to lines 22 (other proceeds) and 23 (costs of obtaining income).
page_pit38_sec4_d: Section D — 19% tax calculation on income, deduction of prior-year losses, and foreign tax paid (proportional credit).
page_pit38_sec4_g: Section G — flat 19% tax on foreign dividends (art. 30a), with credit for withholding tax limited to the double-tax treaty (UPO) rate.
page_pit38_sec4_j: Section J — optional 1.5% OPP request: KRS number, requested amount, detailed purpose, and consent.
page_pit38_sec4_pitzg: PIT/ZG attachment — per-country C.3 rows for foreign share income and related foreign tax; dividends stay in Section G by default.
page_pit38_sec5_step1: Import broker data (Interactive Brokers CSV, IBI Capital PDF) or add transactions manually on the Data page.
page_pit38_sec5_step2: Review the NBP exchange rates — kloPIT automatically fetches the mid-rate from the last business day before each transaction.
page_pit38_sec5_step3: Optionally fill in prior-year losses — up to 50% of a yearly loss, for 5 subsequent years.

page_pit38_sec7_body: kloPIT is a free, open-source PIT-38 calculator that runs entirely in your browser — no signup, no data sent to any server. It handles FIFO, converts to PLN using NBP rates, applies treaty caps to foreign dividends, and fills PIT-38 sections C-G, the payment summary, section J OPP helper, and PIT/ZG C.3 rows.

page_pit38_sec8_item2: Art. 30b PIT Act — taxation of income from the sale of securities (19% rate).

page_pitzg_h1: PIT/ZG — when it is required and how kloPIT handles it
page_pitzg_intro: PIT/ZG is the country-by-country attachment for foreign-source income and foreign tax paid. In kloPIT's PIT-38 view it is generated for share income under art. 30b; foreign dividends stay in PIT-38 section G by default.

page_pitzg_links_lexlege_desc: Convenient article-by-article view of the PIT Act provisions commonly referenced for PIT/ZG, including art. 30b and 45.

page_pitzg_meta_title: PIT/ZG guide — share income and dividends | kloPIT
page_pitzg_sec1_body: PIT/ZG supplements PIT-38 when you need to show foreign-source income and foreign tax paid by country. In the PIT-38 attachment, kloPIT maps share income to PIT/ZG C.3.
page_pitzg_sec2_body: The official PIT-38 flow exposes PIT/ZG C.3 for income under art. 30b, i.e. share and similar capital-market income. kloPIT therefore generates PIT/ZG from sell trades by country.
page_pitzg_sec3_body: Foreign dividends are settled in PIT-38 section G as flat-rate income under art. 30a, with the foreign tax credit shown in positions 47-49. They do not create PIT/ZG entries by default.
page_pitzg_sec3_title: Dividends stay in PIT-38 by default
page_pitzg_sec4_body: A foreign broker, foreign exchange, or foreign trading currency does not by itself create foreign-source capital gains for PIT/ZG. Treaty allocation matters, not where the account is held.
page_pitzg_sec4_title: Why a foreign broker is not enough
page_pitzg_sec5_b1: Real-estate company clauses under OECD art. 13(4).
page_pitzg_sec5_b2: Permanent establishment cases under OECD art. 13(2).
page_pitzg_sec5_b4: Countries without an applicable treaty or with special domestic rules.
page_pitzg_sec5_title: When capital gains can require PIT/ZG
page_pitzg_sec6_body: Foreign tax credit on capital gains matters only when foreign tax actually exists. The income still belongs in your Polish annual return, but PIT/ZG is relevant only if treaty or domestic rules allocate taxing rights abroad.
page_pitzg_sec7_body: kloPIT defaults to the official PIT-38 layout: PIT/ZG is generated for share income, while dividends remain in PIT-38 section G. Enable the dividend compatibility setting only if you intentionally want dividend rows shown in PIT/ZG too.
